title: Percentage of Land Cost in Actual Prices of BTO Flats Constructed in 2016 and 2017
what_it_is: Percentage of Land Cost in Actual Prices of BTO Flats Constructed in 2016 and 2017

sections.label: HDB flat land cost deficit
sections.summary: For 2016 and 2017 projects, land cost was about 60% of development cost, and HDB incurred an average annual deficit of about $1.14 billion from FY2015 to FY2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For projects that were awarded in 2016 and 2017, the land cost was about 60% of total development cost, and this percentage was about the same across 3-, 4- and 5-room flat types.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In general, HDB's total development cost cannot be fully covered from the sale price of the flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is because the pricing of new HDB flats is guided by our objective of keeping public housing affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why in the last three years, from financial year (FY) 2015 to FY2017, HDB incurred an average annual deficit of about $1.14 billion per year for its Home Ownership Programme.

sections.label: HDB land sales and Reserves
sections.summary: HDB is treated like any other developer for land sales, which are benchmarked at a Chief Valuer price and proceeds go to past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Essentially, HDB, as a developer, is treated like any other developer with regard to land sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as Mr Leon Perera and other Members would appreciate, land sales are governed under the Constitutional rules for the protection of Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the sale of land is benchmarked at a price set by the Chief Valuer, and land proceeds go on to past Reserves and we use a share of that through the Net Investment Return contributions that come to the Budget every year.
